newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Record seen for 1997 Queensland sugar crop.
newsitem.headline: Record seen for 1997 Queensland sugar crop.

text.p: Queensland, Australia's main sugar-producing state, could produce another record tonnage of raws in 1997/98 despite a recent cyclone, Harry Bonanno, chairman of grower organisation CANEGROWERS, told the organisation's annual meeting on Tuesday.

The forecast follows industry fears that Cyclone Justin, which flattened large areas of cane in northern Queensland earlier this year, could reduce the state's 1997/98 (June 30) sugar production by around 20 percent.
A record crop in 1997/98 would produce the state's sixth successive record year of sugar production, Bonanno said.

Production in 1996/97 totalled 5.156 million tonnes of 94 net titre sugar, the first time it broke the five million tonnes mark. However, returns for the 1997/98 crop could decline by a further five percent to 10 percent, largely because of depressed world sugar prices, Bonanno said.
Returns in 1996/97 were expected to have fallen by 10 percent to about A$340.00 a tonne, he said. "In the short-term the industry faces a difficult time," he added.
Bonanno was more optimistic about the longer-term.
The world sugar market, which had doubled to 70 million tonnes over the past 10 years, would continue to grow, he said.
"I believe Australia will maintain its position, although GATT has brought little to us," he said.
Bonnano said it was very fustrating for Queensland producers to have to give up Australia's tariff on imported sugar when their international competitors were subsidised.

He said it was preferable for the sugar industry to give up the tariff, in view of the Australian government's competition policy review, so that it could retain single desk monopoly export selling and other industry arrangements.
However, he said it was totally unacceptable for sugar producers in New South Wales (NSW) to receive federal government support after the removal of the tariff when Queensland producers were not.

The CANEGROWERS chief saw some optimism in future world sugar prices being contained within a narrower band with less marginal areas beingt brought into production. Queensland Premier Rob Borbidge added his voice to the attack.
Recommendatioons of the Sugar Industry Review, led by the policy that tariffs on imports be scrapped, were being implemented by the stgate government as a top priority, he said.

But the Queensland government shared CANEGROWERS concern over federal government support for the NSW industry and had written to federal Primary Industries Minister John Anderson on the issue, he said.
Queensland, which produces 95 percent of Australia's sugar, is the world's largest exporter in the world of raw sugar, shipping about four million tonnes in the latest year.
CANEGROWERS' annual meeting is being held in conjunction with the 1997 Australian Sugar Convention.
